name: Eridanus
introduction: is the River, the sixth-largest constellation. It meanders from beside Orion’s foot all the way to brilliant Achernar, deep in the southern sky. In Greek myth, it is the river into which Phaethon fell after losing control of the Sun’s chariot. Northern observers can see only its upper reaches.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Eridanus contains several of our nearest neighbors. [Ran](hip:16537), also called Epsilon Eridani, is a young Sun-like star only 10.5 light-years away, surrounded by rings of dust and at least one giant planet. In 1960, together with Tau Ceti, it was one of the first targets of the search for extraterrestrial radio signals.

[Keid](id:10pc-0109), also called 40 Eridani, is a triple star 16 light-years away. Its white dwarf was one of the first ever identified; science fiction fans may know the system as the home of the planet Vulcan.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Achernar](hip:7588), “the end of the river”, is a hot blue star 140 light-years away. It spins so fast that it is strongly flattened, with an equator far wider than its poles. [Cursa](hip:23875), near Rigel, marks the river’s source.
[Acamar](hip:13847) was once the end of the river, when Achernar was too far south for the Greeks to see. [Rana](hip:17378) is a nearby subgiant, a star beginning to evolve beyond the main sequence.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The Witch Head Nebula, a faint reflection nebula lit by Rigel, lies at the head of the river. Farther away are NGC 1300, a textbook barred spiral galaxy, and the Eridanus Supervoid, linked to a puzzling cold spot in the cosmic microwave background.
